newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany urged to step up fight against corruption.
newsitem.headline: Germany urged to step up fight against corruption.

text.p: German law enforcers on Friday called for concerted action to curb what appears to be a rising tide of corruption in German industry.

Frankfurt senior prosecutor Wolfgang Schaupensteiner, speaking at a conference in Berlin, bemoaned the lack of nationwide co-operation on corruption cases and called for central investigation centres to be set up.
He said bribes paid out each year in the public building industry alone totalled five to ten billion marks.
"Fighting the bribery system is a challenge of the first order for the whole of our society," Schaupensteiner said.
Germany has been hit by a series of corruption scandals in the past year.
A massive investigation, still not concluded, was launched into bribes thought to amount to millions of marks during the construction of Frankfurt airport's second terminal.

This summer the senior management of steel group Thyssen AG was targeted in a fraud probe while the former chairman of failed shipbuilder Bremer Vulkan AG was arrested in June on a funds misuse charges.

Lore Maria Peschel-Gutzeit, head of the Berlin state justice ministry, accused the federal government of a half-hearted approach to tackling corruption and slammed recent proposals on the issue as inadequate.

Describing Bonn as a "toothless tiger" in the fight against industrial corruption, Peschel-Gutzeit said Germany needed to offer milder sentences to individuals involved in, but willing to expose, a corruption ring, thus increasing the chances of breaking up the system sooner.
Peschel-Gutzeit also said public officials accepting any kind of benefit ought to face corruption charges, even when there was no clear evidence of a direct exchange of favours.
